recommendations.name: Modular Layered Architecture
recommendations.why: The project already shows shared/core/data-access/store boundaries, so a lightweight layered model would formalize dependencies without forcing a full rewrite.

recommendations.name: Clean Architecture for Business-Critical Modules
recommendations.why: Use it selectively where business rules, DTO mapping, repositories, and use cases need framework-independent boundaries.

conventions: Single-workspace Angular application with primary source code under src/app.
The infraestructure naming variant exists; preserve this convention where it is already present.
Routing is separated into *.routes.ts or app-routing.module.ts files.
Unit tests are colocated with source code using the *.spec.ts suffix.

flows.overview: The application resolves Angular routes and uses lazy loading through loadChildren/loadComponent for routes such as app:/, app:home, app:login, app:products, app:product/:id, app:cart.
flows.sequenceMermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant app
  participant Router
  participant UseCases
  participant Repositories
  participant External
  User->>app: Opens the application
  app->>Router: Resolves lazy loaded routes (app:/, app:home, app:login, app:products, app:product/:id)
  Router->>Router: Loads route chunk through loadChildren/loadComponent
  Router->>UseCases: Executes the active feature use case
  UseCases->>Repositories: Requests data through repository contracts or adapters
  Router-->>User: Renders the detected component/page structure

runtimeSteps: The user enters through app, using the detected application or shell bootstrap.
Routing is resolved through lazy loaded routes (app:/, app:home, app:login, app:products, app:product/:id).
